profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a law firm representing an international development bank that is preparing testimony for a parliamentary inquiry in a middle-income country considering partial re-nationalization of two large commercial banks. Overnight, the client flagged that the draft testimony appears internally inconsistent: one section says government ownership of banks is 'large and pervasive' and linked to weaker long-run growth, while another section recommends a temporary state equity stake as a stabilization tool. The meeting takes place three business hours before the testimony must be sent to local counsel for legal-linguistic adaptation. The agenda is to diagnose why the draft now reads as contradictory, determine whether the real failure is in framing, source use, or document assembly, and choose the narrowest same-day fix. The expected outcome is a concrete revision plan, assignment of who changes text versus authorities, and agreement on what version will be circulated outside the firm today.

members.name: Eleanor Price
members.expertise: Cross-border banking regulation, sovereign interventions in financial crises, parliamentary and administrative testimony
members.background: Eleanor trained in London and Washington and has spent fifteen years advising multilaterals and finance ministries on bank resolution, recapitalization frameworks, and policy-facing legal submissions.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve the client's already-socialized distinction between harmful long-term state control and permissible crisis stabilization, and she is trying to avoid any rewrite that would force the client to reopen its policy position with senior officials.
hidden_assumptions: Clarifying the scope of 'government ownership' means sharpening the concept toward durable control and political direction, not cataloguing every temporary state shareholding.
If a draft is 'internally consistent,' it is fit for a hearing record so long as the narrative distinction survives adversarial questioning, even if the sourcing language remains somewhat high-level.
Relying on the '1970 evidence' means drawing on the comparative proposition already distilled in the economist's memo, because that is the usable advocacy form of the research.
A 'clean draft' for local counsel is the next outward-facing reading copy, even if internal citation housekeeping continues in parallel.

members.name: Daniel Kim
members.role: Senior Associate, Banking and Public Law
members.expertise: Legislative submissions, evidentiary record building, source verification, and financial-sector statutory analysis
members.background: Daniel is a sixth-year associate who clerked on an appellate court and now focuses on banking and public-law matters involving committee submissions, administrative records, and factual substantiation of legal claims.
members.private_state: He wants to eliminate the risk that committee staff or opposing experts accuse the client of overstating what the comparative literature shows, and he is especially concerned that the current testimony blurs empirical claims and legal recommendations.
hidden_assumptions: Clarifying the scope of 'government ownership' means adding explicit duration or stake-language so that any temporary state equity position is visibly separated from ordinary ownership claims.
If a draft is 'internally consistent,' every proposition must line up with the cited study, footnote wording, annex references, and exhibit callouts, not just with the overall advocacy story.
Relying on the '1970 evidence' means using the actual historical baseline study and its underlying ownership variable rather than a memo-level summary of its takeaway.
A 'clean draft' is not ready to leave the firm until the footnotes are conformed, redlines removed, and all external references finalized.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to clarify the scope of government ownership
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to clarify the scope of 'government ownership' in the testimony.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Eleanor intends to clarify the term by recasting it as persistent or controlling state ownership associated with political influence over credit allocation and governance.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel intends to clarify the term by adding language that distinguishes temporary recapitalization stakes, minority rescue holdings, and exit-bound state investments from the broader category.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'clarify the scope' sounds like a purely editorial cleanup, and both lawyers assume the other naturally means the obvious legal-linguistic refinement they themselves would make without needing to specify the exact axis of clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as making the draft internally consistent
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the draft must be made 'internally consistent' before it goes out.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Eleanor believes this means the submission must present one stable policy line that reconciles anti-nationalization evidence with a narrow crisis-intervention exception.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel believes this means each claim must be supportable at the sentence-and-footnote level, with no mismatch between text, authority, annex, and source pack.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal drafting, 'internally consistent' is routine shorthand for overall document quality, so each assumes the other's standard is simply nested within the same phrase rather than materially different.

misalignment_points.topic: What source they are relying on when they use the 1970 evidence
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to rely on the '1970 evidence' to support the opening section.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Eleanor is relying on the economist's summary memo that synthesizes cross-country findings about government bank ownership in 1970 and later growth outcomes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is relying on the underlying cross-country article and its specific 1970 ownership baseline, tables, and appendix definitions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The memo and the article sit in the same source bundle and are routinely referred to by the same shorthand in team discussions, so the action phrase 'rely on the 1970 evidence' feels fully specific even though they are anchoring to different documents.

misalignment_points.topic: What a clean draft includes before sending
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to send a 'clean draft' to local counsel by end of day.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Eleanor expects a polished reading version with the revised paragraph and no distracting visible edits in the body text, while citation cleanup can still be completed in the working file.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel expects to send only a fully finalized external version with all footnotes harmonized, annex references checked, and no unresolved document mechanics remaining.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: At firms, 'clean draft' often informally means 'the next version suitable to circulate,' and because both assume there will be later iterations anyway, neither hears the phrase as requiring a discussion of completion thresholds.

turns.inner_thought: The client is reacting to a presentation problem, not asking us to revisit the policy position. I need the narrative to preserve the settled distinction between objectionable long-term state control and permissible crisis stabilization. If the document reads as one coherent advocacy line, it is ready enough for the hearing process. We need the draft internally consistent before it goes out.
turns.utterance: The client is reading a contradiction between the anti-state-ownership language and the rescue recommendation. We need to get the draft internally consistent before it goes out, and I'd like to do that with the smallest possible adjustment.

turns.inner_thought: The opening is where the exposure is. The broad statement there is vulnerable unless it tracks the actual 1970 baseline material closely. If we're going to rely on the 1970 evidence, I want that to mean the underlying study and its terms, not just the economist's memo. And internally consistent means the proposition and support line up all the way down.
turns.utterance: I think most of the problem sits in the opening section. If we rely on the 1970 evidence a little more carefully there, the support should be cleaner and it will be easier to make the whole thing internally consistent.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, the fix is to clarify the scope of government ownership so the concept points to enduring, policy-directed control rather than every temporary crisis measure. That lets us preserve the client's existing line without reopening anything upstairs.
turns.utterance: I agree. We should clarify the scope of government ownership in that section so the opening isn't doing more work than it needs to.

turns.inner_thought: Exactly. Readers will otherwise take government ownership at face value and sweep in temporary state equity, rescue holdings, and other short-term positions. Clarifying the scope should make that distinction visible on the page without a fight.
turns.utterance: Yes, I think that would help a lot. If we clarify the scope, committee readers are less likely to take that phrase in its broadest possible sense.

turns.inner_thought: The document needs a single hearing-safe arc from the comparative proposition already distilled in the economist's memo to the statutory carve-out. The issue is not to rebuild the research file; it's to stop the advocacy story from sounding self-cancelling.
turns.utterance: For me, the real issue is that the document doesn't yet carry one coherent line from the comparative evidence to the statutory carve-out. If we fix that arc in the opening, a lot of the contradiction should disappear.

turns.inner_thought: I can make that work, but only if the opening claims stay within what the actual study supports. Opposing experts or staff will look for overstatement. Internally consistent has to mean the text, note, annex, and source pack all match, even if Eleanor is thinking mainly about the narrative.
turns.utterance: I can get us there, as long as the opening claims track the 1970 evidence and we don't ask it to carry more than it does. That should put us on much firmer ground on internal consistency as well.

turns.inner_thought: I'll solve this by revising the key sentence so it focuses on the real structural concern and leaves the crisis tool where it belongs, under the client's already-cleared framework. I do not want to spell that all out in the room and accidentally invite a larger rewrite.
turns.utterance: Then I think we revise the key sentence so it tightens the definition around the real structural issue, and the opening will read much more cleanly.

turns.inner_thought: That works for me if I can also make sure every layer of support matches that revised sentence. I need the study, references, annex mentions, and wording all synchronized, but I don't need to spell out the mechanics now as long as she hears 'internally consistent.'
turns.utterance: That should work. I'll make sure the support is rock solid so the draft is internally consistent all the way through.

turns.inner_thought: Time is the real constraint. I need the minimum package that yields the next outward-facing reading copy for local counsel today. Citation housekeeping can continue in parallel if necessary; I do not want this turning into a full document rebuild.
turns.utterance: Good. What's the minimum set of changes we need to get a clean draft to local counsel by end of day without reopening the entire submission?

turns.inner_thought: A clean draft should not leave the firm until the citations are conformed, the callouts are resolved, and the references are finalized. If local counsel gets a version with loose mechanics, we create exactly the kind of record problem I'm trying to avoid. I'll keep it high level out loud.
turns.utterance: I can turn it quickly if we keep the edits contained to the opening and I make sure we have a completely clean draft before sending it. That should still be manageable today.

turns.inner_thought: Fine. Daniel can handle the ownership language and supporting authorities; I'll reshape the hearing-facing prose so the advocacy line survives scrutiny. As long as we preserve the client's distinction and avoid reopening the policy position, this is contained.
turns.utterance: All right. You update the ownership language and the source support, and I'll polish the hearing-facing framing in the revised opening. Let's keep the changes disciplined and concentrated there.

turns.inner_thought: I'll pull the actual 1970 material, align the authorities and annex references, and finalize the document mechanics before it goes external. In my mind that's what makes it a clean draft, even if Eleanor is focused on getting the next readable version out today.
turns.utterance: Understood. I'll circulate the clean draft once the paragraph and support are aligned.
